label: Birthday party

what_happens.title: What happens at a birthday party
goals: The steps: arrive, say hello and happy birthday, give the present, games, singing and cake, goodbye
Parties can be loud and busy, and that is part of the fun
There is a pick-up time or the grown-up stays
what_happens.parentSkill: Name the party steps in order and say whether you will stay or come back, and when.

who_is_there.title: Who is at the party
goals: The birthday child, their family and the host grown-ups
Other kids, some known and some new
Maybe an entertainer or a costume character
who_is_there.parentSkill: Say who your child already knows at the party and who is in charge.

what_i_do.title: What I do at the party
goals: Say happy birthday and give the present
Join a game or watch first
Ask for a quiet break when it is too much
what_i_do.parentSkill: Practise 'Happy birthday!', 'Can I play?' and 'I need a quiet break.'

if_scared.title: If the party feels too much
goals: Loud music, balloons that pop, many kids, the birthday song
Feeling shy or overwhelmed is okay
Calm tools: a quiet spot, ear muffs, holding a hand, slow breaths, watching first
if_scared.parentSkill: Plan a quiet spot and a signal with your child before the party.

rehearsal.title: Let's practise the party
goals: Wrap the present and make a card
Play a pretend party with toys: hello, game, song, cake, goodbye
Say the steps once more, ending with going home
rehearsal.parentSkill: Have a toy party at home with a song, a game and saying goodbye.

steps: Arrive at the party and say hello
Say happy birthday and give the present
Play games with the other kids
sensory: balloons that squeak and sometimes pop
candles and a smell of cake
lots of kids moving and running
a bright costume or face paint
honestyNotes: Parties can be loud and busy, and balloons can pop. Do not promise the child will have fun or will make friends. Say they can watch first and take a quiet break, and agree with them what happens if they want to leave early.

fallbackAnswer: The birthday child, their family and other kids.
[[GROWNUP]] can tell you who you already know.
[[GROWNUP]] will tell you before the party if they stay or come back.
If [[GROWNUP]] leaves, they come back at pick-up time.

questionButtons.text: What if it is too loud?
fallbackAnswer: Parties can be loud, with music and singing.
You can take a quiet break, cover your ears, or wear ear muffs.
A balloon pop is a loud bang, and then it is over.
It can make you jump, and that is okay.

questionButtons.text: What if I don't want to play?
fallbackAnswer: When you are ready, you can say, can I play?
The present is for the birthday child, because it is their day.
On your birthday, it will be your turn.
Lots of kids feel shy at parties.
You can hold [[GROWNUP]]'s hand and say hello with a wave.
First hello and happy birthday, then games.
Next, the song and cake, and last, goodbye.

techniques.label: Watching first
techniques.how: Let your child watch a game from the side before joining; offer to join with them.

techniques.label: A quiet spot
techniques.how: Find a quiet corner or step outside together for a short break when it gets too much.

techniques.label: Ear muffs or covering ears
techniques.how: Bring ear muffs for the loud parts, like the song or the music.

techniques.label: Holding a hand
techniques.how: Hold your child's hand when arriving and walk in together.

techniques.label: Practising the hello
techniques.how: Practise 'Happy birthday!' and 'Can I play?' at home with toys.

techniques.label: A plan for leaving
techniques.how: Agree a signal and a plan for leaving early if your child needs it, and keep it.

techniques.label: The present job
techniques.how: Let your child choose, wrap and hand over the present; a clear job helps on arrival.

techniques.label: Smell the flower, blow the candle
techniques.how: Breathe in slowly through the nose like smelling a flower and out like blowing a candle.

ritual: Happy birthday and give the present
Song, cake, thank you and goodbye

pain: If your tummy feels wobbly, we can take a break.
If you bump yourself, come to me or the grown-up there.
separation: I will tell you if I stay or come back, and when.
You can find me any time.
unknown: First hello, then games, then song and cake, then goodbye.
strangers: You know some of the kids. Let's say hello together.
The grown-ups there are in charge and can help.
sensory: It is loud. Want a quiet break?
Balloons can pop with a bang. Then it's over.
safety: We have a plan for leaving if you need it.
The quiet spot is right there.
social: You can watch first and join when you are ready.
Lots of kids feel shy at parties.
body: If your body feels too busy, let's take slow breaths.
Tell me if you need the toilet or a drink.
love: I love you, loud or quiet.
I am proud of you for going.
